inputs.agent: the dev VM's production-style system unit opute-bootstrap-mcp.service (Rust 0.3.0 release candidate binary, test identity e2e-devvm-agent, test token), with the Rust k3s provider 1.0.2 from the release (e2e-provider-k3s, port 4320)
inputs.k3s: K3s v1.31.8+k3s1, downloaded by the provider from the K3s GitHub release and checked against its checksums; images pulled by K3s from public registries

requirements.requirement: A K3s server provisioned through typed Host Agent operations
requirements.scenario: The single-node cluster the journey runs on
A client reaches PostgreSQL through the relay with the issued token (the server answers the SSL probe); a wrong token is dropped; a row is written and read back
requirements.spec: the agent's published tools/list (inputSchema, outputSchema, description) for the tool named

requirements.scenario: Secret-bearing input (D24): the relay token is in no durable row
The relay released only with its token; removal leaves no service or data behind
requirements.spec: the agent's published tools/list (inputSchema, outputSchema, description) for the tool named

requirements.scenario: A caller-scoped SQLite database provisioned, reported, refused removal without confirmation, and removed
requirements.spec: the agent's published tools/list (inputSchema, outputSchema, description) for the tool named

steps.guest: chown -R opute /home/opute/.config/opute-e2e && systemd-run --collect --unit=e2e-provider-k3s --uid=opute --gid=opute --setenv=HOME=/home/opute --setenv=OPUTE_PROVIDER_PORT=4320 --property=Restart=no /opt/opute-e2e/providers/opute-provider-k3s >/dev/null && for i in $(seq 60); do ss -ltnH 'sport = :4320' | grep -q . && break; sleep 0.5; done; ss -ltnH 'sport = :4320' | wc -l

python3 -c 'import sys, time, json; sys.path.insert(0, "/opt/opute-e2e/guest"); import mcpwire
for i in range(120):
    r = mcpwire.mcp(3014, sys.argv[1], "tools/list", request_id=i + 1)
    names = [t["name"] for t in ((r.get("body") or {}).get("result") or {}).get("tools") or []]
    if "opute.capability.kubernetes.provision" in names: break
    time.sleep(0.5)
print(json.dumps({"listed": "opute.capability.kubernetes.provision" in names, "tools": len(names), "polls": i + 1}))' '${TOKEN}'

python3 - <<'PY'
import socket
s = socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 15433), timeout=20)
s.sendall(b'${SECRET:relayToken}\n')
s.sendall(bytes([0, 0, 0, 8, 4, 210, 22, 47]))
print((s.recv(1) or b'closed').decode())
PY

python3 - <<'PY'
import socket
s = socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 15433), timeout=20)
try:
    s.sendall(b'not-the-token\n'); s.sendall(bytes([0, 0, 0, 8, 4, 210, 22, 47]))
    print((s.recv(1) or b'closed').decode())
except OSError:
    print('closed')
PY
incus exec e2e-k1 -- k3s kubectl -n e2e-data exec pg-1 -c postgres -- psql -d app -Atqc "CREATE TABLE e2e(note text); INSERT INTO e2e VALUES ('written')"
incus exec e2e-k1 -- k3s kubectl -n e2e-data exec pg-1 -c postgres -- psql -d app -Atqc 'SELECT note FROM e2e'

python3 - <<'PY'
import socket
try:
    socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 15433), timeout=5)
    print('open')
except OSError:
    print('closed')
PY
for i in $(seq 60); do n=$(incus exec e2e-k1 -- k3s kubectl -n e2e-data get clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io,pvc -o name | wc -l); [ "$n" = 0 ] && break; sleep 5; done; echo $n

listen=$(incus config device get e2e-k1 e2e-pg-relay listen) && case "$listen" in tcp:127.0.0.1:*) ;; *) exit 1;; esac; endpoints=$(ss -Hlntp | awk '$4 ~ /^127[.]0[.]0[.]1:/ && /incusd/ {print $4}'); test "tcp:$endpoints" = "$listen"
